direct_answer: Galp does not disclose a transition plan for climate change mitigation as being in place; instead, it states it is “maturing its energy transition plan” and “estimates to publish its energy transition plan upon maturing its portfolio assessment” (no specific adoption/publication date is provided) [Source 1]. Because the plan is not yet published/disclosed, the retrieved passages do not provide evidence that the transition plan is aligned with limiting global warming to 1.5°C [Source 1]. Galp also notes it is reassessing its emission reduction targets while it matures its energy transition plan, but it does not disclose 1.5°C compatibility, a science-based framework/methodology, scenarios, or external assurance for targets in the provided excerpts [Source 9].
compliance_rationale: ESRS E1-1 expects disclosure of the transition plan and, if no plan exists, a timeline for adopting it. Galp indicates it is maturing a plan and intends to publish it, but provides no clear timeline/date [Source 1]. ESRS E1-1/E1-4 also require explaining compatibility with 1.5°C (and related target methodology); the provided passages do not evidence 1.5°C alignment or science-based target details [Sources 1, 9].
disclosure_gaps: Clear statement that a climate change mitigation transition plan is in place (or not) and, if not in place, a specific timeline/date for adoption/publication (only an intention to publish is disclosed) [Source 1].

Explanation of how the transition plan and GHG targets are compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C (Paris-aligned), as required by ESRS E1-1.16(a) (no such explanation in provided passages) [Sources 1, 9].

ESRS E1-4 details on whether targets are science-based and compatible with 1.5°C, including the framework/methodology used, underlying climate/policy scenarios, and whether targets have been externally assured (not evidenced in provided passages) [Source 9].
key_findings: Galp states it is maturing its energy transition plan and expects to publish it after completing a portfolio assessment; no publication/adoption date is disclosed [Source 1].

Galp reports planned capital allocation signals (e.g., ~35% of 2025–2026 gross capex to low-carbon activities) and lists low-carbon project areas, but this does not constitute a disclosed, Paris-aligned transition plan in the provided excerpts [Source 1].
Galp indicates it is reassessing its emission reduction targets as it matures its energy transition plan; no 1.5°C/science-based alignment evidence is provided in the retrieved passages [Source 9].
